Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
David Bayever speaks about codeine addiction and tools that could be of use.

Summary:
Pharmacist David Bayever serves on the SA Pharmacy Council and has been a member of the Central Drug Authority since 2000. He speaks to us about the various issues around codeine addiction, the illicit sale thereof, ways to approach codeine addiction, and an app they're currently developing to assist in better tracking codeine addiction in South Africa.

FULL TRANSCRIPT (with timecode)

00:00:00:14 - 00:00:23:12
Bongani: Before the break, we investigated an alleged codeine smuggling ring, which raises questions around how this opioid is fuelling addiction in many countries. Pharmacist and Wits University lecturer David Bayever serves on the Pharmacy Council and is chairperson of the International Society of Substance Use Professionals. David, welcome to Carte Blanche.

00:00:23:14 - 00:00:24:18
David: Thank you very much, Bongani.

00:00:24:20 - 00:00:38:03
Bongani: I suppose how does the pharmaceutical industry red-flag the kind of thing we saw in that investigation and also, I suppose, those patients who ask for restricted medicines and the pharmacists who cave in?

00:00:39:15 - 00:01:25:25
David: What we need to understand is that the pharmacist has a responsibility to look after the patients in a holistic manner. At the same time, we are the custodians of medicine, and that means that it needs to be controlled from the sale as well as from the manufacturer as well. And these are all the issues that pharmacy is concerned with. So initially what we spoke about, what we speak about, is the fact that when a patient asks for medication, we need to determine whether in actual fact that they are using it for the right reasons, whether it's appropriate for the condition that they're trying to treat, or whether they are using it to deal with some other issues, such as a psychological issue, which they might be trying to mask, or that they are using this medication as a coping mechanism to deal with their other problems.

00:01:26:04 - 00:01:58:22
David: So those are the red flags that we are looking for. As pharmacists, we are trained and we are sponsored by pharmaceutical companies and media, such as, for example, the Brave Campaign, which is run as a media campaign sponsored by a manufacturer - Adcock in this particular instance - who are giving out information, not only to the pharmacists on how to deal with the problem, but also to the public to make them aware of the dangers associated with the inappropriate use of medication, in other words, the misuse of medication.

00:01:58:24 - 00:02:01:07
Bongani: There's no pharmacist who can say they didn't know.

00:02:01:25 - 00:02:13:15
David: Absolutely not. The biggest problem we have, of course, is that when the patient confronts them, we have to be able to deal with the patient in a holistic manner without being punitive at the same time.

00:02:14:04 - 00:02:18:21
Bongani: Someone might say, look, what's the big deal? This is over the counter medicine in any case.

00:02:19:17 - 00:02:57:08
David: I think we need to go one step back, then, and understand what this whole issue is around the dependence and addiction. And we need to recognize that we are dealing with three different elements over here. The one is firstly the agent, which is the medicine, or in other words, in their particular case, the drug, and the effect that it can have on them if it is taken in the wrong dose, for the inappropriate use, or for the wrong reasons. So that's the agent. The second one, of course, is the environment that they find themselves in and the circumstances that they may be in, which are things that we really can't deal with and we can't change.

00:02:57:10 - 00:03:04:08
David: But these have an effect on the reasons why they are using or looking for something chemical to help them feel different.

00:03:04:10 - 00:03:08:09
Bongani: How do you help someone who is not willing to recognize their addiction?

00:03:08:11 - 00:03:41:22
David: Well, we have a program which has been put out which has been tested. The problem is that it has never been enforced. The program will treat the problem by, on a single cloud, recording every single movement of those codeine-containing preparations. In other words, directly from the manufacturer, where it is initially made, to the wholesaler, to the pharmacy, and eventually to the end user. And all that information gets stored on one single system for the entire country.

00:03:42:04 - 00:04:00:15
David: Now, this will give the pharmacist an ability to be able to recognize those patients who are at risk or who might have a predisposition based on their genetic makeup. And then in order to be able to inform them about the dangers that could be lurking in their misuse and abuse of the substance.

00:04:00:17 - 00:04:22:13
Bongani: Clearly, some work to be done there. Appreciate your time for joining us this evening. Now, for those in need, the International Society of Substance Use Professionals is developing a free app to help you manage mental health and addiction issues. We've also put together a short guide on identifying codeine addiction. You can find that now on the Carte Blanche website.
